title_en: Yichang Maternal and Child Health Hospital v. Yichang Administration for Industry and Commerce — dispute over administrative penalty decision
keywords_en: administrative; unfair competition; administrative penalty; first instance; basic people's court; Hubei Province; state organ; legal person; Anti-Unfair Competition Law; Whether a public institution qualifies as an operator under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law; determination of secretly accepting kickbacks off the books; whether the administrative penalty procedure is lawful; dismissal of claims; drug procurement; accepting kickbacks; commercial bribery; administrative litigation
full_text_en:
Yichang Maternal and Child Health Hospital v. Yichang Administration for Industry and Commerce — Administrative Penalty Dispute

Plaintiff: Yichang Maternal and Child Health Hospital, Hubei Province. Address: No. 118, Yiling Road, Yichang City, Hubei Province.

Legal Representative: Yao Changben, President of the Hospital.

Agents ad litem: Zhang Pei, Vice President of the Hospital; Yao Zhicheng, lawyer from Hubei Xiling Law Firm.

Defendant: Yichang Administration for Industry and Commerce, Hubei Province. Address: Erguo Er Road, Yichang City, Hubei Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Yong, Director of the Administration.

Agents ad litem: Sun Changwei and Cai Yixin, officials of the Administration.

The Administrative Penalty Decision, Yi Shi Gong Shang Chu Zi (2000) No. 027, rendered by the Defendant, Yichang Administration for Industry and Commerce, Hubei Province (hereinafter referred to as the AIC) on February 11, 2000, determined the following: During its drug procurement activities, the Plaintiff, Yichang Maternal and Child Health Hospital, Hubei Province (hereinafter referred to as the Maternal Hospital), accepted payments and goods from 10 drug distribution enterprises, including Yichang Pharmaceutical Company, in 26 instances, totaling 58,721.58 yuan. This conduct violated Article 8, Paragraph 1 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Anti-Unfair Competition Law) and Article 2, Paragraph 1 and Article 4 of the Interim Provisions of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce on Prohibiting Commercial Bribery (hereinafter referred to as the Interim Provisions), constituting an act of unfair competition. Pursuant to Article 22 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, the Maternal Hospital was fined 10,000 yuan.

The Plaintiff, the Maternal Hospital, dissatisfied with this administrative penalty decision by the Defendant, the AIC, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Xiling District People's Court of Yichang City, Hubei Province.

Plaintiff's Allegations:
1.  The Defendant's administrative penalty decision contains errors in fact-finding and the application of law.
    (1) Among the 26 instances of payments and goods totaling 58,721.58 yuan that the Defendant found the Hospital to have accepted, the finding regarding the acceptance from the Business Department of Angel Bio-Pharmaceutical Company is erroneous. After accepting a donation of 15,900 yuan from the Business Department of Angel Bio-Pharmaceutical Company on July 9, 1999, the Hospital returned 7,846.39 yuan to the said Business Department on December 17 of the same year. This refund should be deducted from the total amount of payments and goods accepted. Therefore, the actual amount accepted by the Hospital should be 50,875.19 yuan, not 58,721.58 yuan.
    (2) All accepted payments and goods have been lawfully recorded in the Hospital's financial accounts. This constitutes a disclosed discount and does not fall under commercial bribery. Even if issues regarding an inappropriate discount ratio or incorrect accounting entries exist, they should not be investigated and dealt with by the administrative authority for industry and commerce.
    (3) The Hospital is a public welfare institution fully funded by the state budget, not an operator capable of being a market entity. Therefore, it is not within the regulatory scope of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law.
2.  The Defendant's administrative penalty decision involves procedural violations.
    (1) The entity notified for inspection in the Defendant's "Notice of Inspection" was "Yichang Maternal and Child Health *Hospital*" [using a different Chinese character for "Hospital"], not our "Yichang Maternal and Child Health Hospital". The Defendant's investigation of our Hospital using this "Notice of Inspection" constitutes an error in the investigated entity.
    (2) The Defendant's administrative penalty decision only records the total amount of donations accepted by the Hospital but fails to mention the evidence upon which this amount is determined.
    The Hospital requests the court to annul this administrative penalty decision according to law and order the Defendant to bear all litigation costs of this case.

The Plaintiff, the Maternal Hospital, submitted the following supporting evidence:
1.  The legal person registration certificate for public institutions held by the Maternal Hospital.
2.  The "Decision on Health Reform and Development" issued by the Central Committee of the CPC and the State Council on January 15, 1997.
3.  A set of receipts for the payments accepted by the Maternal Hospital in this case, along with sample bank cash payment slips.
4.  A detailed list of the payments and goods accepted in this case by the Maternal Hospital.
5.  A certificate from the Yichang Red Cross regarding the donation of drugs to the Maternal Hospital.
6.  The social organization legal person registration certificate of the Yichang Red Cross.
7.  "Hubei Province Implementing Measures for the Red Cross Society Law of the People's Republic of China".

Defendant's Defense:
1.  While the payments and goods totaling 58,721.58 yuan accepted by the Plaintiff during drug procurement activities from November 1998 to August 1999 were entered into the unit's own financial accounts, the accounts used did not truthfully or accurately reflect the cost of drug procurement. In essence, this conduct constitutes the clandestine acceptance of kickbacks off the books.
2.  The Plaintiff, as the buyer in drug procurement activities, is not a consumer itself. The purchased drugs are resold to patients. Although the Plaintiff is a fully state-funded medical and health institution, its daily business activities are compensated. Its drug procurement behavior constitutes a commercial operation and falls within the scope of regulation under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. In accordance with Article 4 of the SAIC's Interim Provisions and the spirit of Document Gong Shang Gong Zi (1996) No. 127 jointly issued by the SAIC, the Ministry of Health, the State Pharmaceutical Administration, the State Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine, and the State Council Office for Rectifying Unhealthy Practices, the administrative authority for industry and commerce has the power to investigate and punish the acceptance of kickbacks and other commercial bribery conduct by medical and health institutions in drug procurement activities, pursuant to the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Therefore, the administrative penalty decision imposed by our Administration on the Plaintiff has clear facts and correctly applies the law. The People's Court should uphold it.

The Defendant, the AIC, submitted the following supporting evidence:
1.  The administrative penalty decision, Yi Shi Gong Shang Chu Zi (2000) No. 027, and the service receipt.
2.  The "Notice of Administrative Penalty Decision" (Gong Shang Shu Zi (2000) No. 27) made on February 1, 2000, and its service receipt.
3.  The case filing approval form completed on November 3, 1999.
4.  The "Final Investigation Report on the Case of Commercial Bribery by Yichang Maternal and Child Health Hospital" (enclosing a detailed list of payments and goods accepted by the Hospital) prepared on November 16, 1999.
5.  Records of inquiries conducted on November 2, 8, and 9, 1999, with Wu Qing'e, Zhang Pei, Cao Min, and Wang Yongqing of the Maternal Hospital, respectively.
6.  Other income accounts of the Maternal Hospital for 1998 and 1999.
7.  Sample accounting vouchers and receipts for payments and goods accepted by the Maternal Hospital.
8.  Sample drug sales invoices from the Business Department of Yichang Sanxia Pharmaceutical Factory.
9.  The "Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China".
10. The "Hubei Province Anti-Unfair Competition Regulations".
11. The SAIC's "Interim Provisions on Prohibiting Commercial Bribery".
12. The Hubei Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce's reply dated October 19, 1998, regarding the "Inquiry on Whether Hospitals are Subjects Regulated by the Anti-Unfair Competition Law".
13. Documents jointly issued by the State Administration for Industry and Commerce, the Ministry of Health, the State Pharmaceutical Administration, the State Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine, and the State Council Office for Rectifying Unhealthy Practices: Gong Shang Gong Zi (1996) No. 127, Gong Shang Gong Zi (1997) No. 91, and Gong Shang Gong Zi (1998) No. 66.
14. Document Guo Ban Fa (1999) No. 75 from the General Office of the State Council.

Facts Found by the First Instance Court:

The Xiling District People's Court of Yichang City, Hubei Province, found through trial that:

The Plaintiff, the Maternal Hospital, is a fully state-funded public health institution providing services to the general public, offering medical specialties such as internal medicine, surgery, obstetrics and gynecology, pediatrics, dermatology, medical aesthetics, and stomatology. From November 1998 to August 1999, during its drug procurement activities, the Maternal Hospital accepted payments totaling 54,921.58 yuan from 10 drug distribution enterprises, including Yichang Pharmaceutical Company, in 25 instances, and accepted one air conditioner valued at 3,800 yuan. The total amount accepted was 58,721.58 yuan. The payments and goods accepted were recorded in the Hospital's financial accounts under the "other income" and "fixed assets" accounts, respectively. In November 1999, the Defendant, the AIC, discovered this issue during an inspection of the Maternal Hospital's drug procurement activities. After filing a case and conducting an investigation, on February 1, 2000, the AIC served the "Notice of Administrative Penalty Decision" (Gong Shang Shu Zi (2000) No. 27) upon the Maternal Hospital. The Maternal Hospital did not exercise its right to present statements or defenses within the statutory period. On February 11, the AIC issued the administrative penalty decision Yi Shi Gong Shang Chu Zi (2000) No. 027. Based on the finding that the Maternal Hospital's conduct in accepting payments and goods violated Article 8, Paragraph 1 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, and Article 2, Paragraph 1 and Article 4 of the Interim Provisions (SAIC Order No. 60 (1996)), and pursuant to Article 22 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, the AIC decided to impose a fine of 10,000 yuan on the Maternal Hospital. On February 13, the administrative penalty decision was served on the Maternal Hospital. The Maternal Hospital, dissatisfied, initiated this lawsuit.

Opinion of the Xiling District People's Court of Yichang City, Hubei Province:

The Plaintiff, the Maternal Hospital, claimed that it had returned 7,846.39 yuan of the 15,900 yuan accepted from the Business Department of Angel Bio-Pharmaceutical Company, and therefore, this refund should be deducted from the total amount of payments and goods accepted. Consequently, the total amount should be 50,875.19 yuan, not 58,721.58 yuan. This claim by the Maternal Hospital is inconsistent with its own account records, and it failed to provide relevant evidence to support it. Therefore, this claim cannot be sustained. The Defendant's finding that the Maternal Hospital accepted a total of 58,721.58 yuan in payments and goods is correct.

Article 2, Paragraph 3 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law states: "For the purposes of this Law, 'operators' refer to legal persons, other economic organizations, and individuals engaged in the production or sale of goods or the provision of paid services (hereinafter 'goods' includes services)." This provision collectively refers to legal persons, other economic organizations, and individuals engaged in the production or sale of goods or the provision of paid services as operators, without distinguishing the economic nature of the operators. Although the Plaintiff, the Maternal Hospital, is a fully funded public welfare health institution, its business activities include providing medical services and selling drugs, both of which are compensated. Therefore, its drug procurement and sale constitute commercial activities. Furthermore, Article 8, Paragraph 1 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law provides: "Operators shall not use property or other means to bribe in order to sell or purchase goods. Anyone who, secretly off the books, gives a rebate to the other party, whether a unit or an individual, shall be deemed to have offered a bribe; anyone who, secretly off the books, accepts a rebate from the other party, whether a unit or an individual, shall be deemed to have accepted a bribe." The "other party, whether a unit or an individual" mentioned here is not exclusively limited to operators; it includes all units and individuals who accept rebates secretly off the books while engaging in official procurement activities. The Maternal Hospital's drug procurement is one of its official activities. In engaging in this activity, the Maternal Hospital qualifies as an operator under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. The Maternal Hospital's argument that it is not subject to the Anti-Unfair Competition Law is unfounded.

Article 8, Paragraph 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law states: "When selling or purchasing goods, an operator may offer discounts to the other party in an express manner and may pay commissions to intermediaries. An operator who offers discounts to the other party or pays commissions to intermediaries must truthfully record them in the books. An operator who accepts discounts or commissions must truthfully record them in the books." The term "rebate" refers to cash or material goods given to or accepted by the other party secretly off the books due to procurement or sales activities. The term "discount" refers to a price concession offered or accepted during the purchase or sale of goods in an express manner and truthfully recorded in the books. Although both involve the giving or receiving of certain economic benefits in business activities, the difference lies in the fact that rebates are conducted secretly off the books, and the parties involved tend to avoid openly acknowledging the connection between the rebate and the business activity. In contrast, discounts are conducted in an express manner and truthfully recorded in the books, with no need for the parties to conceal the connection between the discount and the business activity. The term "books" referred to here means the accounts established in accordance with the financial accounting system that can truthfully reflect business activities, not any other accounts. Although the Plaintiff, the Maternal Hospital, recorded the payments and goods accepted from drug distribution enterprises during drug procurement activities in its books, the entries were not made in the operational accounts reflecting drug procurement activities but in other types of accounts. This method of recording cannot truthfully reflect the connection between the acceptance of payments/goods and the drug procurement, cannot reflect the actual cost of the purchased drugs, and cannot truthfully reflect the business activities between the parties. Therefore, for the drug business activities, the acceptance of payments and goods through this method remains "off the books" and "clandestine." The Defendant's finding that the Maternal Hospital's conduct constitutes the clandestine acceptance of kickbacks off the books is correct. The Maternal Hospital's claim that this constitutes an express discount is unfounded. Article 22 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law provides: "Where an operator uses property or other means to bribe in order to sell or purchase goods, if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if it does not constitute a crime, the supervisory and inspection department may impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan, depending on the circumstances, and shall confiscate any illegal gains if any." The AIC's imposition of a 10,000-yuan fine on the Maternal Hospital is legally based.

The entity listed as the subject of inspection on the "Notice of Inspection" issued by the Defendant was "Yichang Maternal and Child Health *Hospital*" [using a different character], which differs slightly from the Plaintiff's official name. The facts investigated and punished by the AIC did indeed occur at the Maternal Hospital. Regarding the facts investigated and penalized by the AIC, the Maternal Hospital does not deny their relevance to itself, aside from the unsubstantiated claim of having returned 7,864.39 yuan to the Business Department of Angel Bio-Pharmaceutical Company. Therefore, there is no issue of an error in the investigated entity. The discrepancy in the entity name on the "Notice of Inspection" is, in fact, a clerical error.

Although the administrative penalty decision prepared by the Defendant only states the facts of the violation without listing the evidence supporting those facts as required by the Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China, this evidence existed at the time the penalty was imposed. Moreover, the Plaintiff only disputes the legal characterization of the facts, not the existence of the facts themselves. This indicates that the administrative penalty decision suffers from issues of improper drafting and incomplete content.

In conclusion, the administrative penalty decision, Yi Shi Gong Shang Chu Zi (2000) No. 027, rendered by the Defendant, the AIC, clearly ascertains the facts and correctly applies the law. While it has the issue of improper drafting, this does not constitute a violation of legal procedure and should be upheld. Based on this, the Xiling District People's Court of Yichang City, Hubei Province, rendered the following judgment on July 7, 2000:

The administrative penalty decision, Yi Shi Gong Shang Chu Zi (2000) No. 027, of the Defendant, the AIC, is upheld.
The litigation costs of this case, 200 yuan, shall be borne by the Plaintiff, the Maternal Hospital.

The Maternal Hospital, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Yichang Intermediate People's Court, Hubei Province. Grounds for appeal:
1.  The appellant is a fully state-funded health institution, using drugs for the purpose of providing medical and health services to society, not for the disguised sale of drugs. The appellant engages in non-profit public welfare undertakings, and any income generated is used to supplement the insufficiency of fiscal appropriations. The donations accepted by the appellant are not required to be recorded in the drug inventory books as per regulations; therefore, there is no issue of secretly accepting kickbacks off the books.
2.  The first-instance judgment erroneously applied the law by finding the appellant to be an operator regulated by the Anti-Unfair Competition Law and that it had secretly accepted kickbacks off the books.
3.  The first-instance judgment, on one hand, acknowledges that the administrative penalty decision is improperly drafted and lacks complete content but, on the other hand, states that it does not violate legal procedure. This is contradictory.
4.  Furthermore, the appellee failed to conduct a hearing procedure before imposing the administrative penalty, which blatantly violates the provisions of the Administrative Penalty Law.
    The appellant requests the annulment of the first-instance judgment and revocation of the appellee's administrative penalty decision.

The appellant, the Maternal Hospital, submitted the following evidence in the second instance:
1.  "Implementation Opinions on Classified Management of Urban Medical Institutions" issued by the Ministry of Health, the State Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine, the Ministry of Finance, and the State Development Planning Commission on July 18, 2000.
2.  The "Request for Instructions on the Accounting Treatment of Drug Discount (Donation) Income" submitted by the Maternal Hospital to the Yichang Municipal Finance Bureau on July 18, 2000, and the Bureau's reply to this request on August 11, 2000.
3.  "Accounting System for Hospitals" and "Financial System for Hospitals" issued by the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Health.
4.  "Accounting System for Public Institutions" and "Financial Rules for Public Institutions" issued by the Ministry of Finance.
5.  "Notice on Relevant Provisions for Medical and Health Units Implementing the New Accounting System" issued by the Hubei Provincial Department of Finance and the Hubei Provincial Department of Health on March 10, 1999.
6.  "Notice on Strengthening the Management of Medical Fees and Drug Procurement Activities" issued by the Hubei Provincial Department of Health on October 19, 1999.
7.  "Yichang City Drug Price Management Regulations" issued by the Yichang Municipal Price Bureau on August 24, 1999.
8.  Sample supply agreements (6 copies) signed by the Maternal Hospital with drug distribution enterprises such as the Business Department of Yichang Sanxia Pharmaceutical Factory on January 1, 1999.

The appellee, the AIC, argued in its defense:
1.  The appellant's procurement and sale of drugs are both compensated activities, essentially constituting commercial activities. The "other party, whether a unit or an individual" stipulated in Article 8, Paragraph 1 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law does not exclude legal persons of public institutions.
2.  The appellant accepted payments and goods from drug distribution enterprises without reducing the drug procurement costs, instead recording them under other income and fixed assets. This conduct has lost the nature of a discount, becoming the commercial bribery of secretly accepting kickbacks off the books.
3.  The fine imposed on the appellant by the appellee is 10,000 yuan, which does not require the application of hearing procedures.
4.  The first-instance judgment has clear findings of fact and correctly applies the law and should be upheld.

Supplementary evidence submitted by the appellee to the second-instance court:
1.  Sample supply agreements (5 copies) signed by the Maternal Hospital with drug distribution enterprises such as the Business Department of Yichang Sanxia Pharmaceutical Factory on January 1, 1999.
2.  The medical institution practice license of the Maternal Hospital.
3.  The self-inspection and self-correction report on rectifying unhealthy practices in pharmaceutical procurement and distribution made by the Maternal Hospital on October 20, 1999.
4.  The "Self-Inspection and Self-Correction Registration Form for Discounts in Drug and Equipment Procurement Since 1998" completed by the Maternal Hospital on August 30, 1999. (Note: All of the above evidence was examined in the first-instance trial but not submitted to the first-instance court; it was submitted upon the request of the second-instance court).
5.  The "Interim Rules on Administrative Penalty Hearings for Administrative Authorities for Industry and Commerce" formulated by the State Administration for Industry and Commerce.

After hearing the case, the Yichang Intermediate People's Court, Hubei Province, confirmed that the evidence numbered 5, 6, and 7 provided by the appellant, the Maternal Hospital, in the first instance was irrelevant to this case and could not serve as the basis for determining the facts. Apart from this, the procedures for obtaining and the methods for compiling the other evidence submitted by both the Maternal Hospital and the appellee, the AIC, were lawful and could serve as the basis for determining the facts of the case. The facts identified in the second instance based on valid evidence are the same as those in the first instance. It was also found that the trial procedures of the first-instance court were lawful, and neither party raised any objections to the trial procedures of the first-instance court.

Opinion of the Yichang Intermediate People's Court, Hubei Province:

The entities regulated under Article 2, paragraph 3 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law include not only operators who are approved for registration and hold business licenses, but also other legal persons, other economic organizations, and individuals who engage in business activities or for-profit services or other activities related to market competition. Although the Appellant Health Care Institution is a non-profit public health institution fully funded by the government budget, its daily business activities are profit-making, and such activities are business conduct related to market competition, which should be regulated in accordance with the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Standardizing the business conduct of the Health Care Institution according to law does not affect its use of profits from operations to make up for the shortfall in government funding, as it claims. The Health Care Institution's argument on appeal that it is a non-profit institution fully funded by government budget and that its income is used to offset insufficient government appropriations, and therefore should not be subject to the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, cannot be sustained.

The Appellant Health Care Institution, relying on evidence submitted during the second instance, argues that its accounting for the money and goods received complies with financial regulations. Upon examination, this evidence only shows how donations received should be accounted for, and does not address how rebates or discounts received should be accounted for. Donations are a different concept from rebates or discounts. Donations can occur at any time and are gratuitous; they cannot be conditional on the recipient making a return for the donor's business activities. In contrast, rebates or discounts occur during business operations and are means used by operators to facilitate transactions. The party receiving a rebate or discount must complete a transaction with the operator to obtain it. Although the Health Care Institution labeled the money and goods received as "donations," this cannot conceal the truth that it received these funds and items as a result of completing drug transactions. If the Health Care Institution had not completed drug transactions with the pharmaceutical distribution enterprises, those enterprises would not have made such "donations" to the Health Care Institution. Therefore, the money and goods received by the Health Care Institution in this case are not donations. The Health Care Institution's argument that it correctly accounted for the money and goods received in this case by following the rules for accounting for donations is untenable. Since the Health Care Institution, although it entered the received money and goods into its accounts, did not do so truthfully, it failed to meet the requirement of "express and truthful accounting" for discounts. Consequently, the Health Care Institution's argument on appeal that these sums and items were disguised discounts or high discounts is also unsupportable.

The Appellee Industrial and Commercial Bureau, as the specialized supervisory and inspection authority, before imposing the penalty on the Appellant Health Care Institution, filed the case, conducted investigation and evidence collection, served a penalty notice, and informed the Appellant of its right to present statements and defenses. Its penalty procedure complies with legal provisions. The penalty decision issued by the Industrial and Commercial Bureau did not specifically list the names of the evidence relied upon to determine the existence of the Health Care Institution's illegal acts, making the content of the penalty decision incomplete. This constitutes a minor flaw in the administrative act. This administrative flaw by the Industrial and Commercial Bureau did not reach the degree of infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of the counterparty in administrative management and does not affect the valid establishment of the penalty decision. Therefore, it cannot be determined that the Industrial and Commercial Bureau's administrative act was procedurally illegal.

Article 42 of the Administrative Penalty Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Before an administrative organ makes a decision to order suspension of production or business, revoke a permit or license, impose a relatively large fine, or other administrative penalty decisions, it shall inform the party of the right to request a hearing; if the party requests a hearing, the administrative organ shall organize a hearing." With reference to the provisions of Article 6, paragraph 3 of the "Interim Rules on Administrative Penalty Hearings for Industry and Commerce Administrative Organs" formulated by the State Administration for Industry and Commerce, an industry and commerce administrative organ shall inform a legal person or other organization of the right to request a hearing when imposing a fine of RMB 50,000 or more. The fine imposed by the Appellee Industrial and Commercial Bureau on the Appellant Health Care Institution was RMB 10,000, which does not meet the standard of a "relatively large fine" under the Administrative Penalty Law and, according to law, the hearing procedure is not required to be applied. The Health Care Institution's appeal argument that the Industrial and Commercial Bureau's failure to apply the hearing procedure violated the Administrative Penalty Law is also untenable.

The Appellee Industrial and Commercial Bureau, based on the verified facts and in accordance with Article 22 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, imposed a fine of RMB 10,000 on the Appellant Health Care Institution. The application of the law was correct, and the amount of the fine was within the statutory range. The first-instance judgment, which upheld the administrative penalty decision made by the Industrial and Commercial Bureau, correctly ascertained the facts, had sufficient evidence, correctly applied the law, and followed lawful procedures. Accordingly, the Yichang Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province, on November 21, 2000, rendered the following judgment:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 200 shall be borne by the Appellant Health Care Institution.
